tasks.title: Orchard Harvest Windows
tasks.prompt:
An orchard schedules harvest windows for 6 rows of apple trees. Each window is defined by a start time and an end time, both in minutes since midnight. Two windows overlap if they share any minute.

The windows are:
Row A: start 420, end 510
Row B: start 480, end 600
Row C: start 570, end 660
Row D: start 700, end 780
Row E: start 750, end 840
Row F: start 840, end 930

Write a program that for each row prints how many minutes of that row's window overlap with at least one OTHER row's window, and then prints the total combined unique working minutes across all rows.

Output exactly 7 lines.

For each row in order A through F, print:
Row X: OOO min overlap
where X is the row letter and OOO is a 3-digit zero-padded count of minutes in that row's window that are also inside at least one other row's window.

Then print:
UNIQUE TOTAL: UUU min
where UUU is a 3-digit zero-padded count of minutes from minute 0 to minute 1439 that fall inside at least one window.

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

tasks.title: Beekeeper Honey Extraction
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper extracts honey from 7 hives. Each hive yields a number of full jars and a partial jar measured in seconds (a full jar takes 300 seconds to fill). Write a program that processes the following yields and prints a summary.

Hive yields (jars, partial seconds):
Hive 1: 12 jars, 0 partial seconds
Hive 2: 8 jars, 145 partial seconds
Hive 3: 15 jars, 210 partial seconds
Hive 4: 10 jars, 0 partial seconds
Hive 5: 6 jars, 275 partial seconds
Hive 6: 14 jars, 30 partial seconds
Hive 7: 9 jars, 180 partial seconds

For each hive, compute total seconds = jars * 300 + partial seconds. A partial jar counts as a full jar only if its partial seconds equal 300 (none do here), so full jars for reporting = jars (partial never reaches 300 in this data).

Print exactly 9 lines:

For each hive 1 through 7, one line:
Hive N: SSSS sec -> J jars
where N is the hive number, SSSS is a 4-digit zero-padded total seconds, and J is the whole number of full jars from that hive (just the jars value).

Then two summary lines:
TOTAL SECONDS: SSSSS
FULL JARS: JJJ
where SSSSS is a 5-digit zero-padded sum of all hives' total seconds, and JJJ is a 3-digit zero-padded sum of all jars.

No trailing spaces on any line.

tasks.title: Library Book Due Times
tasks.prompt:
A library lends books for exactly 14 days (20160 minutes). When a book is returned late, the fine is 25 cents per started hour of lateness. Write a program that processes 6 books.

Each book has: checkout minute, return minute (both minutes since midnight of the return day, i.e. lateness is computed as return_minute + days_late * 1440 - 20160, but for this exercise all books are returned on the same day as shown).

Book data (checkout minute, return minute):
Book 1: checkout 540, return 600
Book 2: checkout 600, return 635
Book 3: checkout 660, return 700
Book 4: checkout 720, return 805
Book 5: checkout 780, return 845
Book 6: checkout 840, return 925

For this exercise, treat lateness as (return_minute - checkout_minute - 20160) minutes; since all values are small, lateness will be negative, meaning the book was returned BEFORE the due time in this simplified model. Instead, use this rule: lateness = max(0, (return_minute - checkout_minute) - 1440) minutes (books are due 1 day after checkout for this exercise). Fine = ceil(lateness / 60) * 25 cents if lateness > 0, else 0.

Wait — simplify: each book is due at checkout_minute + 1440 minutes (next day same time). Lateness = return_minute + 1440 - (checkout_minute + 1440) = return_minute - checkout_minute - 1440... 

FINAL RULE: For each book, lateness_minutes = max(0, (return_minute - checkout_minute) - 60). Books are due 60 minutes after checkout in this express-lending program. Fine = ceil(lateness_minutes / 60) * 25 cents if lateness_minutes > 0, else 0.

Print exactly 8 lines:

For each book 1 through 6:
Book N: LLL min late -> $F.FF
where LLL is 3-digit zero-padded lateness minutes and F.FF is fine in dollars with 2 decimal places.

Then two summary lines:
TOTAL LATE MINUTES: LLLL
TOTAL FINES: $T.TT
where LLLL is 4-digit zero-padded sum of all lateness minutes and T.TT is sum of fines with 2 decimal places.

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

tasks.title: Beekeeper Foraging Distance

A beekeeper tracks foraging trips from the hive. Each trip has a departure time and return time in seconds, and a distance in meters. Bees fly at 8 meters per second.

Trip 2: dep 10, ret 50, dist 320
Trip 3: dep 20, ret 65, dist 400
Trip 4: dep 30, ret 80, dist 480
Trip 5: dep 40, ret 75, dist 280
Trip 6: dep 55, ret 95, dist 340

For each trip compute duration = ret - dep, and check whether the bee could have flown the stated distance at 8 m/s: possible = (duration * 8 >= distance).

For each trip 1 through 6:
Trip N: DDD sec, EEE m, OK/SHORT
where N is trip number, DDD is 3-digit zero-padded duration, EEE is 3-digit zero-padded distance, and OK if possible else SHORT.

POSSIBLE: P of 6
